newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end lower on bank liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end lower on bank liquidation.

text.p: Taiwan money rates sank at mid-session on Wednesday as banks continued to liquidate excess funds, but dealers expected the decline to be limited by the central bank's tightening measures.
The overnight interbank rate ended at 5.995 percent against Monday's 6.229 close, with 30-day commercial paper at 5.95-6.00 percent against 6.25.
The central bank on Wednesday issue T$5 billion in negotiable certificates of deposit to mop up excess liquidity before the upcoming two-day holiday on March 29-30.
Dealers expected the short-term rates to stabilise at current levels, still well outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone.
Central bank Governor Sheu Yuan-dong told parliament on Monday that the central bank would not continue to issue NCDs "blindly" but would react appropriately to market conditions.

The central bank has made major NCD issues almost every day of the past two weeks, aiming to soak up some of the loose liquidity that many analysts have said was a main force fuelling the stock market's dramatic rise.
The bond market saw no transaction in afternoon trade.
The 10-year 86/4 bond yield ended the morning session at 6.0875 percent against 6.0900.
